text.tspan: Route 53 health checks: endpoint, calculated, CloudWatch alarm
• interval 30 s, or 10 s (fast, extra cost)
• connect in 4 s, respond in 2 s after connect
• optional string match in first 5,120 bytes
healthy if ALL (AND), ONE OR MORE (OR) or at least x of y
children are healthy · up to 255/256 children
use: maintenance without failing every check
Health check watches the alarm's data stream:
data: choose healthy / unhealthy / last known)
Use for private resources: checkers are outside the VPC
Firewall: allow inbound from Route 53 health checker IPs
How health checks drive DNS failover
• Attach a health check to records (failover, weighted, latency, geolocation, geoproximity, multivalue...): unhealthy ones are left out.
• A record with no health check is always treated as healthy. If every record in the group is unhealthy, Route 53 treats them all as healthy.
• Alias records: set Evaluate Target Health = Yes so the alias follows the health of the ELB / records it points to.
• HTTPS checks don't validate the TLS certificate. Health checks run on a schedule, not when a query arrives. They publish CloudWatch metrics.
